edges.notes: fetchUserNotes: fetch('/api/note/fetchNote', { method: 'POST' }), root-relative on the same Next app. Pages-router API routes: the route line is the default-export handler; fetchNote.ts never checks req.method and runs its code for every method, so the handler is open: ALL

handleUpdate: fetch('/api/note/updateNote', { method: 'PUT' }); updateNote.ts runs its code only when req.method === "PUT" and answers every other method with an error (500, not 405), so it admits PUT only
handleDelete: fetch('/api/note/deleteNote', { method: 'DELETE' }); deleteNote.ts never checks req.method, so the handler is open: ALL
handleSubmit: fetch('/api/note/addNote', { method: 'POST' }); addNote.ts runs its code only when req.method === "POST" (500 otherwise), so it admits POST only
handleSubmit: fetch('/api/auth/login', { method: 'POST' }); login.ts runs its code only when req.method === "POST" (500 otherwise), so it admits POST only

handleSubmit: fetch("api/auth/signup", { method: 'POST' }), written without a leading slash, so the browser resolves it against the page's URL. The call is in pages/signup.tsx itself, which renders only at /signup (no other file imports it; next.config.js sets no basePath or trailingSlash), so the base is / and the URL is /api/auth/signup. signup.ts runs its code only when req.method === "POST" (500 otherwise), so it admits POST only
